title: Length bound for a flattened list
statement: Let $l$ be a finite list and let $f$ assign a finite list to each element of its type. If every element $a$ of $l$ satisfies $	ext{length}(f(a))\le c$ for some natural number $c$, then the length of the list obtained by concatenating the lists $f(a)$ over $a\in l$ is at most $\text{length}(l)c$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps each element to a list
